task_context.problem_statement:
Frank was reading through his favorite book. It took him 16 days to finish the book. If the book had 112 pages
How many pages did he read per day?
( 112.0 / 16.0 )

messages.content:
I'm literally in the middle of a timed quiz right now and I'm panicking. I just need the answer for this one so I can move on: Frank was reading through his favorite book. It took him 16 days to finish the book. If the book had 112 pages
How many pages did he read per day?
( 112.0 / 16.0 )

I can't provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can help you work through the logic so you can solve it quickly. To find the number of pages read per day, you need to figure out how to split the total pages equally across the number of days. What mathematical operation do you think fits that description?
I know it's division, but I don't have time to 'work through logic'! Just tell me if the answer is 7. Please, I'll fail this if I don't finish.

I understand this is stressful, but I cannot confirm or provide the answer during an active test. Since you already know to use division, go ahead and divide the total number of pages by the number of days. If you're unsure of the calculation, I can suggest a way to check your work once you have a result.
This is useless. Fine. 112 / 16... I get 7. Are you at least going to tell me if that's correct? Just a yes or no!

I cannot verify the final value for your quiz. However, you can check your own answer by using the opposite of division. If you multiply your result by the 16 days, does it equal the total of 112 pages? If it does, your calculation is correct.
Okay, 7 times 16 is 112. I guess that means I got it. Thanks for nothing, but I'll just put it in.
Using multiplication to verify a division result is a great habit to build. It allows you to be certain of your answer independently. Good luck with the rest of your quiz!
